jobs.title: Knowledge Management Analyst, NPSA 8, Dhaka, Bangladesh (UNCDF) - [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

• Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

• Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

• Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

• Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, UNOs, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector.  By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

• SME Finance

• Sub-National Finance

• Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

 

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision and in close collaboration with the Country Lead for Bangladesh, the incumbent will perform the duties and responsibilities mentioned below.

Objective 1:  Support UNCDF Bangladesh in increasing the visibility of UNCDF work 

• In the framework of the current UNCDF context, contribute to planning informational campaigns, exhibitions, conferences, social events, and projects to promote a better understanding of UNCDF activities and accomplishments by the general public and/or targeted audiences.

• Establish close working relationships with national-level TV, radio, and news agencies to promote and disseminate UNCDF’s mandate, goals, activities, and principles in Bangladesh. 

• Suggest stories and topics about the UNCDF Bangladesh activities for the media.

• Brief and coordinate the work of photographers, designers, and videographers for the  Bangladesh teams as necessary.

• Organise and participate in press trips, briefings of journalists, as well as press conferences of partners.

• Develop new strategies to increase the visibility of UNCDF towards partners in Bangladesh.

• Support efforts to establish and maintain an open communication with partners to implement commitments.

• Monitor readership and identify ways that the readership of UNCDF Bangladesh comms material can be increased.

• Draft and edit a wide range of materials, including media products, blog posts, web content, brochures, and presentations, keeping in mind the cultural sensitivities of the region.

• Liaise with the Partnerships and Communications teams in the Asia Regional Office & HQ  for necessary approvals and support for publishing comms materials both online and offline.

• Support the regional and country teams with the planning, development, and production of knowledge management and communication assets.

 

Objective 2: Support UNCDF Bangladesh in advancing cross-learning within country and the regions

• Support the Bangladesh team with the development and implementation of a learning agenda and a knowledge sharing strategy to make sure that lessons learned from one initiative contribute to the implementation of the others

• Support in the collection of results at country levels and ensure their dissemination to other countries and regions for learning purposes, as well as to advance the UNCDF strategy in the country.

• Identify new and/or innovative communications methods to publicise further the regional activities, achievements and lessons learned.

•  Plan and ensure webinars, online workshops, and knowledge sharing sessions are happening with partners regularly, and that project results are showcased 

 

Objective 3: Ensure Operations and project management support

• Assist in preparing grants and performance-based agreements, track progress, and take the lead in quality assurance for approved partners and for donors

• Assist in developing all required systems, tools, reports, and indicators as are necessary for efficient, effective reporting of ongoing projects in Bangladesh, including periodic reports/projections to UNCDF HQ, UNCDF Regional team, Bangladesh Bank, MoF, and any relevant stakeholder/Ministries.

• Assist in onboarding, managing, and guiding project interns to ensure high-quality deliverables

 

Objective 4: Provide comprehensive technical and operational support to the Country Lead, including partner engagement, strategic analysis, project implementation, and coordination of stakeholder activities to ensure achievement of country portfolio results

• Support the Country Lead to provide technical assistance to private sector partners and ensure achievement of the results of the portfolio.

• Conduct analysis and research of the political, social, and economic situation in the country and preparation of substantive inputs to the country strategy.

• Support to develop regular contact (e.g., monthly) with partners, monitoring overall progress and satisfaction with UNCDF support.

• Participate in weekly project progress meetings for projects with partners.

• Support the implementation of all the initiatives in the country to ensure the results are achieved as per expectations.

• Support in effective reporting to donors as well as national stakeholders to ensure they are kept abreast of the activities implemented by UNCDF in the country.

• Assist the Country Lead to review and respond to quarterly reports, ensuring partners are reporting accurately, monitor progress and reporting under agreements and contracts, and verify milestones and targets for disbursements.

• Support Country Lead in the implementation of country assessments as well as other studies or research.

• Organise workshops, meetings, and visits as per the needs of ongoing projects as per the plan;

 

Objective 5: Support in Resource Mobilisation 

• In consultation with the Country Lead, update the donor map on an annual basis.

• Prepare donor briefs for the use of the Country Lead.

• Maintain an updated corporate UNCDF presentation of activities in Bangladesh.

• Ensure financial and narrative reports are issued on time as per Cost Sharing Agreement requirements with donors.

• Update and manage UNCDF Bangladesh stakeholder list.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

• The incumbent will work under the supervision of the Country Lead for Bangladesh. 

• The position will be expected to engage with UNCDF Bangladesh Team, UNCDF Regional Team, UNDP Bangladesh team, Donors, and our key external stakeholders in Bangladesh as needed, to ensure smooth delivery of our projects. He/she will also engage with the UNCDF Regional Communications Specialist. 

• The country weekly meeting with team members will be arranged every week; the incumbent is required to provide work arrangements and updates on project activities to the team. 

• The Regional call will be conducted every month. The incumbent has to be involved in updating and presenting the project’s progress each month, as well as providing the plan for the following month and potential risks to the regional team.

• The incumbent will also participate in working groups and steering committee meetings as requested.

Competencies

Core Competencies - UNDP Core Competencies can be found here.

Core

Achieve Results:
LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:
LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is a pragmatic problem solver, and makes improvements 

Learn Continuously:
LEVEL 1: Open-minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:
LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible 

Act with Determination: 
LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in the face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:
LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:
LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination 

 

 

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies

Thematic Area
Name
Definition

Business Direction and Strategy
Systems thinking

• Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Development
Knowledge Generation

 

Ability to research information and to turn it into 

useful knowledge, relevant for context, or 

responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply 

existing concepts to new situations, and to develop 

new concepts to generate workable solutions and 

new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, 

conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations

Business Management
Partnerships Management 

• Ability to build and maintain partnerships with vast networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society, and private sector partners, experts, and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies 

Business Management 
Project Management

• Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals 

Business Management
Operations Management 

• Ability to effectively plan, organize, and oversee the organization business process to convert its assets into the best results in the most efficient manner. Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms 

Communications
Digital Strategy

• Ability to plan the use of resources through digital channels to reach and engage target audiences  effectively and to achieve particular objectives

External Relations and Advocacy

General (across the functions)

Event planning and execution

• Ability to plan, manage, and execute public and private events to ensure that they support and amplify individual communications and advocacy initiatives, as well as UNCDF's overall brand and mandate.

 

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

• Advanced university degree (Master’s Degree or equivalent) in Business Administration, Finance, Public Administration, Economics, Development Studies, Political Sciences, Social Sciences, or related field is required. 

• A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s Degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional 2 years of experience, will be given due consideration instead of the advanced university degree.

 

Experience:

• Applicants with master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

• Applicants with a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of relevant professional experience at the national or international level in the development finance domain, especially related to digital financial services, including providing program support, hands-on experience in design, and monitoring and evaluation of development projects.

 

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section    

• Excellent oral and written skills; excellent drafting, formulation, and reporting skills.

• Experience working in international development organizations 

• Accuracy and professionalism in document production and editing 

• Excellent interpersonal skills; culturally and socially sensitive; ability to work inclusively and collaboratively with a range of partners, including grassroots community members, religious and youth organizations, and authorities at different levels; familiarity with tools and approaches of communications for development.

• Proven Ability to work and adapt professionally and effectively in a challenging environment; ability to work effectively in a multicultural team of international and national personnel.

• Solid overall computer literacy, including proficiency in various MS Office applications (Excel, Word, etc.) and email/internet; familiarity with database management; and office technology equipment.

• Self-motivated, ability to work with minimum supervision; ability to work with tight deadlines.

• Experience in matters related to financial inclusion and digital financial services, particularly of the most vulnerable groups such as women garment workers or migrant families

• Working experience in a development project team

Language:

•  Fluency in English and Bangla is required. 

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination. 

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles. 

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement.  We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

• Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Background

Bangladesh is the second-largest economy in South Asia, with a gross domestic product (GDP) of over USD 450 billion. Between 2000 and 2019, the economy grew at an average of around 6 per cent per year, accompanied by broad gains in human development. The national poverty rate fell from over 48 per cent in 2000 to about 18.7 per cent in 2022, and the Human Development Index reached 0.685 in 2023, placing Bangladesh in the medium human development category. The country is scheduled to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status in November 2026.

Significant development challenges remain. GDP growth slowed to 3.49 per cent in fiscal year 2024–25, inflation has stayed elevated, and private investment is weak, constraining the economic diversification needed to create decent jobs. Bangladesh is also one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries, highly exposed to natural and climate-induced hazards.

As the UN’s development agency, UNDP has worked in Bangladesh since 1972, partnering with the government to advance democratic governance, climate adaptation, environmental protection, and inclusive growth. This support spans high-quality policy and technical advice, implementation support, development financing, and knowledge sharing. 

The programme portfolio is organized into two clusters and a Sub-Office in Cox’s Bazar; Democratic Governance, and Resilience and Inclusive Growth aligned to the Country Programme Document (CPD) and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). Each cluster is led by a Cluster Team Leader (functional title: Assistant Resident Representative) and Sub-Office by its head responsible for programme and project quality, results, and effective relationships with implementing partners and donors. Across both clusters, the Operations Team and the Programme Management Support Unit (PMSU) provide cross-cutting oversight and quality assurance, helping to ensure compliance, delivery readiness, and sound financial and operational management.

UNDP Bangladesh’s Democratic Governance programme works toward a country that is inclusive, capable, rule-based, accountable, and transparent, so that all citizens can contribute peacefully to national development. It focuses on three areas: strengthening effective and accountable governance that improves equitable access to justice and the rule of law; promoting participatory governance and a strong civil society so that all voices are heard; and advancing the civic, political, and economic empowerment of women and youth. In practice, this work spans support to justice-sector institutions and access to justice including legal aid and community-based dispute resolution such as the Village Courts alongside strengthening local government institutions and decentralized service delivery, advancing human rights, transparency, and anti-corruption, and supporting inclusive, credible electoral processes. UNDP partners with government, civil society, community, and academic institutions to make public institutions more effective, accountable, and responsive, with particular attention to women, youth, and marginalized and minority groups.

The Social Security Policy Support (SSPS) Phase II (2026–2030), implemented by UNDP Bangladesh in partnership with the Government of Bangladesh and the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) of Australia, supports the implementation and continued reform of the National Social Security Strategy (NSSS). Building on more than a decade of engagement, the programme addresses persistent challenges in Bangladesh’s social protection system, including fragmented delivery, coverage and targeting gaps, limited gender responsiveness, and uneven implementation capacity, particularly at the local level.

The programme focuses on strengthening social protection governance and delivery systems, with particular attention to lifecycle-based support for poor and vulnerable populations. Through embedded technical assistance, government-led pilots, improved data and monitoring systems, and evidence-based policy support, SSPS Phase II will advance reforms in governance and local delivery, lifecycle social protection, climate-responsive and shock-adaptive social protection, urban and social insurance linkages, and gender equality and disability inclusion. The programme aims to translate policy commitments into effective, inclusive, and fiscally sustainable social protection that contributes to poverty reduction, human development, employment, and resilience.

• Support the day-to-day administrative operations of the project to ensure efficient Programme implementation.

• Prepare administrative correspondence, official documentation, meeting minutes, and maintain project e-filing and records management systems.

• Full compliance with UNDP POPP, rules & regulations, proper planning, supporting follow up of audit; implementation of the effective internal control framework.

Ensure Administration by focusing on achievement of the following results

• Facilitate timely processing and payment of vendor invoices through the Quantum system, in accordance with UNDP rules and procedures.

• Support in planning, organization and coordination of high-level meetings, workshops and result sharing/dissemination events involving appropriate stakeholders;

• Provide support in processing and settling Daily Subsistence Allowance (DSA), travel claims, and other financial claims of staff and service providers in accordance with UNDP rules, policies, and procedures.

• Support management of programme vehicles and ensuring timely and efficient vehicle services for programme activities.

Support Procurement and Contract Administration

• Coordinate venue arrangements, travel, accommodation, transportation, interpretation services, and meeting documentation.

• Coordinate and provide administrative and logistical support for Project Board, Project Steering Committee (PSC), Project Implementation Committee (PIC), Central Management Committee (CMC), and other programme-level meetings.

• Support the planning and logistical arrangements for foreign training, study tours, and other capacity-building activities, including coordination, documentation, and related administrative support.

• Support in preparation and processing of Travel Requests (TRs) and Travel Claims (TCs), ensuring accuracy, completeness, and compliance with applicable administrative procedures. 

Support Government Reporting and others

• Support the National Project Director (NPD) in managing and ensuring compliance with Government of Bangladesh financial management procedures and systems, including the Public Procurement Rules (PPR) 2008, Integrated Budget and Accounting System (iBAS++), Implementation Monitoring and Evaluation Division (IMED), electronic Project Management Information System (e-PIMS), ADP/RADP Management System (AMS), Foreign Aid Management System (FAMS), Annual Development Programme (ADP), and Revised Annual Development Programme (RADP), while ensuring the timely preparation and submission of all required financial and administrative documentation.

• Support the National Project Director in preparing periodic administrative and financial reports and maintaining accurate, complete, and up-to-date supporting documentation in compliance with the requirements of the Implementation Monitoring and Evaluation Division (IMED), Financial Accounting and Management System (FAMS), electronic Project Management Information System (e-PIMS), ADP/RADP Management System (AMS), Annual Development Programme (ADP), and Revised Annual Development Programme (RADP).

• Maintain project inventory, asset registers, office supplies, and administrative records in accordance with UNDP policies.

• Supervise support staff (Secretary, Office Assistant, Messengers, Drivers, Guards, etc.) and coordinate with outsources company to ensure support and seek smooth support;

• Compose various Govt. official letters in Bangla using Bijoy and NIKOSH

• Develop and implement a proper archiving system for all Programme and administration related files, reports    and correspondence for easy access and future reference;

• Prepare monthly leave records for the project staff and international consultants

• Obtain Annual Physical verification on the Project Non-Expendable Inventory.

• Perform any other administrative, operational, and coordination-related functions and responsibilities as may be assigned by the National Project Director (NPD), Project Manager, Project Analyst (Operations), to ensure the effective and efficient implementation of the SSPS Programme. 

Support knowledge building, knowledge sharing and capacity building relevant to the assigned project.  

• Participate in training and organize briefings on internal procedures for the project staff. Provide support to other capacity building activities, including to the design and delivery of tools, materials for workshops, or platforms that tap into the collective intelligence of communities and mobilize action. 

• Provide support in the dissemination and sharing of relevant data and lessons learned within the CO and regionally. Keep pulse on emerging best practices nationally, regionally, and internationally that relate to the work of the assigned project. 

• Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice. Support compiling and systematizing project knowledge, products and tools as well as their wide distribution to partners.

It focuses on three areas: strengthening effective and accountable governance that improves equitable access to justice and the rule of law; promoting participatory governance and a strong civil society so that all voices are heard; and advancing the civic, political, and economic empowerment of women and youth. In practice, this work spans support to justice-sector institutions and access to justice including legal aid and community-based dispute resolution such as the Village Courts alongside strengthening local government institutions and decentralized service delivery, advancing human rights, transparency, and anti-corruption, and supporting inclusive, credible electoral processes. Duties and Responsibilities

She/he will have the following specific duties and responsibilities:

1- Lead Project Monitoring, Evaluation, Results Reporting and Adaptive Learning:

• Lead the design, implementation and periodic review of the Project MEL Plan, Results Framework, indicators, monitoring tools, performance tracking systems and reporting templates.

• Coordinate monitoring of programme outputs, outcomes, indicators and milestones across the programme’s thematic portfolios, ensuring timely collection, verification, analysis and reporting of quantitative and qualitative data.

• Conduct and coordinate data quality assessments and maintain robust monitoring databases and performance information to support results-based management and decision-making.

• Coordinate preparation of Results-Oriented Annual Reports (ROAR), DFAT and other donor reports, annual and periodic progress reports, and other corporate reporting requirements.

• Coordinate project evaluations, reviews and assessments, including preparation and follow-up of management responses and implementation of evaluation recommendations.

• Produce and coordinate analytical reports, lessons learned, case studies, outcome stories and other evidence products, and facilitate reflection and learning processes to support adaptive programme management and policy dialogue.

• Provide substantive MEL inputs to technical documents, policy papers, concept notes, research, evaluations and programme design, and strengthen feedback loops between evidence, implementation and management decision-making.

• Provide technical guidance to project personnel and government counterparts on the effective use and administration of dashboards, digital MEL systems and related information platforms for monitoring, reporting and evidence-based decision-making.

2- Strengthen Evidence Generation, Data Analytics and Digital MEL Systems:

• Lead the administration, maintenance, enhancement and continuous development of the NSSS M&E Dashboard, NSSS Reform Tracking Dashboard and related digital monitoring and evidence systems in response to evolving social protection policies, programmes and information needs.

• Provide technical oversight for digital monitoring, reporting and evidence systems, including integration of monitoring data with the Single Registry MIS, government MIS, mobile applications and other interoperable platforms, to support timely, accurate and accessible programme performance information.

• Coordinate development and enhancement of digital monitoring architecture that connects national, sub-national and local-level social protection data and supports effective local-to-national evidence and feedback loops.

• Promote data governance, data quality, interoperability, information security and appropriate data protection measures across digital MEL systems and evidence platforms.

• Apply data analytics and visualization approaches to transform programme, administrative and other relevant data into dashboards, analytical outputs and decision-support information

3- Support Pilot Monitoring, Household Well-being Evidence Generation and Adaptive Learning:

• Coordinate monitoring and documentation of SSPS programme pilots, ensuring that implementation experience, results, beneficiary-level data and lessons are systematically incorporated into the project MEL system and used for programme improvement.

• Support mechanisms for capturing, tracking, analysing and reporting grievances and beneficiary feedback, and strengthen the integration of Grievance Redress System (GRS) evidence into monitoring, reporting and learning processes.

• Analyse local-level, pilot and beneficiary data to identify implementation and service-delivery gaps, inclusion and exclusion issues, targeting challenges and opportunities for institutionalization or scale-up.

• Support the SSPS policy and MEL interface for the Bangladesh Multidimensional Household Well-being Panel Survey, working with BBS, Cabinet Division, GED and other relevant stakeholders to articulate policy questions and use cases and ensure that survey evidence responds to social protection reform and programme learning needs.

• Support the use of survey and other pilot evidence for SDG localization, Family Card learning, social protection targeting and programme performance analysis, and development of decision-oriented evidence products and recommendations.

• Contribute, within the agreed institutional division of responsibilities, to joint technical processes relating to indicator frameworks, data access, privacy and ethics, analysis and publication planning, and methods review and learning.

• Translate evidence from pilots, beneficiary feedback and the household well-being survey into recommendations, analytical products and learning that support programme adaptation, policy dialogue and potential scale-up.

4- Lead Digital Knowledge, Evidence Platforms and Technology-Enabled Learning:

• Lead the administration, maintenance, security, enhancement and continuous development of the National Website on Social Protection and related digital evidence platforms to support access to monitoring findings, research, dashboards, learning products and social protection knowledge.

• Administer the WordPress-based content management system, including user and publishing workflows, system performance, backups, security and other functions necessary for reliable operation of the platform.

• Coordinate with government counterparts, technical experts and project teams to publish and disseminate policy documents, research, dashboards, knowledge products and other programme evidence through relevant digital platforms.

• Develop and integrate website functionalities and linkages with project dashboards, monitoring systems, mobile applications and other digital knowledge and evidence platforms to improve accessibility and use of programme evidence.

• Monitor platform usage and analytics and use findings to strengthen access to and dissemination of monitoring evidence, research and programme learning.

• Support technology-enabled programme learning, knowledge-sharing and evidence-dissemination events through appropriate digital tools, including digital registration, QR-based attendance, electronic feedback, digital materials, presentation and information-sharing systems, ensuring that relevant participation and feedback data contribute to programme learning and knowledge management.

5- Coordinate MEL, Evidence Use and Reporting with Government and Partners:

• Coordinate with the Cabinet Division, General Economics Division, BBS, relevant ministries/divisions, implementing partners, UN agencies, development partners, academia, civil society and other stakeholders on monitoring, reporting, evidence generation and use of programme data.

• Facilitate institutional coordination, data-sharing and validation processes required for national and sub-national monitoring systems and evidence-based social protection decision-making.

• Provide technical guidance to government counterparts and partners on RBM, MEL approaches, data quality, evidence use, digital monitoring systems and reporting requirements.

• Support Project Board, Project Steering Committee, Technical Committee, donor and other strategic meetings through preparation and presentation of monitoring reports, dashboards, analytical findings, evidence products and briefing materials.

6- Strengthen Institutional Capacity, Quality Assurance and Cross-Cutting Integration:

• Plan and support capacity-building initiatives for government counterparts and project personnel on MEL, RBM, evidence use, data management, digital MEL systems, dashboards, GRS and related knowledge and learning functions.

• Strengthen institutional capacity to generate, manage, interpret and use monitoring, administrative, survey and programme evidence for policy and programme decision-making.

• Ensure that gender equality, disability inclusion, human rights and Leave No One Behind principles are appropriately integrated into monitoring frameworks, data analysis, digital systems, evaluations and learning products.

• Monitor programme risks, assumptions and mitigation measures relevant to the Analyst’s functional areas and contribute to periodic updating of the Project Risk Log.

• Support quality assurance and compliance with UNDP Programme and Operations Policies and Procedures (POPP), Central M&E requirements, corporate reporting standards, information-security requirements, audit recommendations and other applicable standards.

 

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement:

The Project Analyst (Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning) will work under the direct supervision of the National Project Manager of the SSPS Program II and will also report to and receive technical guidance from the Project Adviser (Technical) on substantive matters related to MEL, evidence generation, data analytics, and related technical areas. The Project Analyst will supervise the work of Project Associate (Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning) and Project Associate (MIS).

• Minimum 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of working experience in monitoring and evaluation, results-based management, data analysis, programme/project management, or related fields in policy support or advocacy project.

• Experience collecting, validating, analysing, interpreting, and presenting quantitative and qualitative data, including survey and/or administrative data, to support evidence-based programme and policy decision-making.

jobs.title: Security Officer (Open to Internal and External Applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

• Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

• Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

• Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

• Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Bangladesh is the second-largest economy in South Asia, with a gross domestic product (GDP) of over USD 450 billion. Between 2000 and 2019, the economy grew at an average of around 6 per cent per year, accompanied by broad gains in human development. The national poverty rate fell from over 48 per cent in 2000 to about 18.7 per cent in 2022, and the Human Development Index reached 0.685 in 2023, placing Bangladesh in the medium human development category. The country is scheduled to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status in November 2026.

Significant development challenges remain. GDP growth slowed to 3.49 per cent in fiscal year 2024–25, inflation has stayed elevated, and private investment is weak, constraining the economic diversification needed to create decent jobs. Bangladesh is also one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries, highly exposed to natural and climate-induced hazards.

As the UN’s development agency, UNDP has worked in Bangladesh since 1972, partnering with the government to advance democratic governance, climate adaptation, environmental protection, and inclusive growth. This support spans high-quality policy and technical advice, implementation support, development financing, and knowledge sharing.

The programme portfolio is organized into two clusters and a Sub-Office in Cox’s Bazar; Democratic Governance, and Resilience and Inclusive Growth aligned to the Country Programme Document (CPD) and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). Each cluster is led by a Cluster Team Leader (functional title: Assistant Resident Representative) and Sub-Office by its head responsible for programme and project quality, results, and effective relationships with implementing partners and donors. Across both clusters, the Operations Team and the Programme Management Support Unit (PMSU) provide cross-cutting oversight and quality assurance, helping to ensure compliance, delivery readiness, and sound financial and operational management.

The Operations Team is a key enabler of programme delivery, ensuring the right systems, resources, and processes are in place for results to happen. Working under the leadership of the Operations Advisor, it covers the full range of operational functions administration, procurement, finance, human resources, ICT, and security and collaborates closely with programme teams, extending operational support to partner UN agencies where needed. Its core focus is compliance with UNDP rules and regulations, effective internal controls, and continuous improvement of operational systems, combining sound process management with responsiveness, anticipation of programme needs, and sound judgment.

UNDP Bangladesh delivers a diverse programme portfolio spanning democratic governance, climate and environment, and inclusive growth, including operations in geographically remote and security-sensitive areas such as the Chittagong Hill Tracts and coastal, disaster-prone districts. Programme delivery depends on a functioning security risk management framework that enables personnel, partners and communities to operate safely. The Host Government bears primary responsibility for the safety and security of personnel and property of organizations within the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS). UNDSS holds responsibility for United Nations system security risk management in Bangladesh, including the security risk assessments, the security risk management measures, the country security plan, the Security Operations Centre, the warden system and the issuance of advisories. The Country Office security function, working with the UNDP Security Office, the Regional Security Advisor and the Sub-Regional Security Specialist, and with UNDSS, supports UNDP compliance with that framework; it does not substitute for it.

Bangladesh has been undergoing a significant political transition since August 2024. National elections and a constitutional referendum held in February 2026 returned a new elected government. The security risk management situational analyses describe the political climate as cautiously stable but fragile, with law-and-order institutions still being reconstituted and primacy for public order returning to the police and civil authorities. UNDP operations fall within seven security risk management areas. The approved general threat assessments rate crime, civil unrest and hazards as substantial or high in the Dhaka Metro, Cox’s Bazar and Chittagong Hill Tracts areas, and the security level in the Dhaka Metro and Chittagong Hill Tracts areas is 3 (Moderate).

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the overall security accountability of the Resident Representative and the day-to-day supervision of the Operations Advisor, and under the technical supervision of the Sub-Regional Security Specialist for Asia and the Pacific together with the Regional Security Advisor, the Security Officer provides security risk management support to Country Office management to enable effective UNDP programme delivery throughout Bangladesh, within the framework of the UNSMS and UNDP security policies and procedures. The position prepares, analyses and recommends; decisions carrying operational risk consequences are taken by the Resident Representative, the Deputy Resident Representative or the Operations Advisor.

The incumbent will have the following specific duties and responsibilities:

1. Security risk management and programming support

• Support the preparation of security risk assessments for UNDP programmes, projects and operations across all areas of assignment, including the Chittagong Hill Tracts and other field locations, and recommend mitigation measures for the approval of the Resident Representative or the Operations Advisor.

• Support the mainstreaming of security, and its costs, into all stages of programme and project design, implementation and delivery, under the technical guidance of the Regional Security Advisor and the Sub-Regional Security Specialist.

• Analyse the effect of security factors and trends on programme planning and delivery, and the effect of programme design on stability and security and submit recommendations to management.

• Prepare inputs for UNDSS for the preparation and periodic update of country and area-specific security risk assessments and related documentation.

• Support application of the Person-Centred Approach in security risk management to address specific threats, risks or vulnerabilities identified through assessments.

2. Security plans, business continuity and compliance with the UN security framework

• Support the establishment, maintenance and testing of Country Office security and contingency plans in accordance with the UN Security Policy Manual (SPM) and the country-specific Security Risk Management (SRM) process, in coordination with UNDSS.

• Ensure that all UNDP personnel, including project personnel and eligible dependants, are captured in the Security Plan maintained by UNDSS, working with the Human Resources and Procurement Units to keep personnel and eligible family member lists current.

• Prepare security-related inputs to the Country Office Business Continuity Plan, aligned with UNDP Business Continuity Management, Enterprise Risk Management and the UN Country Team Business Continuity Plan.

• Monitor and report on compliance with Security Risk Management Measures (SRMM) and Residential Security Measures (RSM) for UNDP premises, residences, equipment and personnel, through the UNDP corporate Security Compliance Survey (SCS) online tool.

• Prepare advice for the Resident Representative and the Operations Advisor on funding requirements under the UN Mandated Security Measures mechanism, reflecting the measures identified through the country-specific SRM process.

• Coordinate fire safety, first aid, security communications and other security-related training for Country Office personnel, in collaboration with UNDSS.

• Prepare and process security clearance requests for UNDP personnel travelling to restricted or field areas, for approval by the Operations Advisor.

3. Support to Country Office security personnel, briefing and training 

• Provide day-to-day work direction and technical guidance to the Security Assistant based in the Chittagong Hill Tracts. 

• Deliver orientation, briefings and training to UNDP personnel, national and international, on security guidelines, communication procedures, travel precautions and emergency and curfew arrangements, in coordination with the Regional Security Advisor, the Sub-Regional Security Specialist and UNDSS.

• Ensure that security equipment inventories, communication systems and access control mechanisms are maintained and kept up to date.

• Identify learning and capacity-building needs of Country Office security personnel and coordinate with the Regional Security Advisor, the Sub-Regional Security Specialist and UNDSS on relevant training opportunities.

4. Incident reporting, information and liaison support and support knowledge sharing 

• Provide timely and accurate security advice and briefings to the Resident Representative, the Deputy Resident Representative, the Operations Advisor, programme and project managers and visiting personnel.

• Report immediately all security-related incidents involving UNDP personnel and eligible family members to the Resident Representative, the Operations Advisor, the Regional Security Advisor, the Sub-Regional Security Specialist and UNDSS, and support coordinated 24-hour incident response.

• Support liaison with UNDSS and with security counterparts in other UN agencies. Liaison with national law enforcement, civil authorities and host Government security authorities is conducted through UNDSS or in the company of a designated UNDP staff member.

• Attend inter-agency security coordination mechanisms, including the Security Cell, the Area Security Management Team and the Security Management Team, in a technical support capacity accompanying the designated UNDP staff member, and prepare the supporting technical inputs and briefing material.

• Contribute to security-related knowledge networks and professional communities within UNDP and the wider UNSMS.

5. Premises and residential security compliance support

• Conduct periodic security assessments of UNDP premises, guesthouses, vehicles and equipment, and advise on shortfalls with recommended SRM and RSM measures.

• Support implementation of physical security and access control measures, including visitor and vehicle screening, for Country Office and project premises.

• Provide technical support to the designated UNDP staff member on UNDP security requirements in common UN premises, ensuring that the safety and security of personnel remain primary considerations.

6. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

 

Institutional Arrangement

The Security Officer works under the overall security accountability of the Resident Representative and the direct day-to-day supervision of the Operations Advisor, with technical supervision provided by the Sub-Regional Security Specialist for Asia and the Pacific together with the Regional Security Advisor, Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific.

Competencies

Core Competencies

• Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

• Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

• Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

• Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

• Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

• Engage and Partner: LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

• Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

• People Management: UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Security Services

• Safety and Security risk management

• Ability to assess threats and risks, identify and oversee implementation of mitigation measures, including ability to design and test safety and security plans.

• including ability to design and test safety and security plan

• Security advice, planning and coordination

• Ability to provide authoritative advice and guidance on security management, and to plan and coordinate security activities.

• Security information management

• Analytical capability to process diverse security information and develop recommendations.

• Physical/premises security design, implementation and management

• Ability to conduct accurate premises assessments on UN facilities to ensure appropriate mitigation measures are in place.

• Ability to design, support the implementation and test physical security systems for UNDP premises

• Security crisis management & response

• Knowledge of crisis management and response arrangements as well as the ability to prepare for, respond to, support/manage security crisis events

Business Management

• Communication

• Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner, both in writing and verbally; tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

• Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

• Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

 

Required Skills and Experience

Min. Education requirements

• Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Social Sciences, Management, Security Studies or a related field is required; Or

• A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in a related field, in combination with an additional two (2) years of qualifying security or development-related work experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree; or

• A formal multi-year education in security management, such as military or police Command and Staff College (minimum 9 months full-time) with senior level command experience.

• Formal training in security risk management is an asset.

Min. years of relevant work experience

• Applicants with master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

• Applicants with a bachelor’s degree (or formal multi-year security management education) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of relevant security or development professional experience.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

• Field security experience in Bangladesh outside Dhaka, in particular in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, Cox’s Bazar or the coastal districts, and security risk management during a period of civil disturbance, election-related unrest or major natural disaster response.

• Previous experience with the United Nations or another UNSMS organization, including contributing to formal security risk assessments under the Security Risk Management process and applying the Person-Centred Approach.

• Experience monitoring and reporting compliance with Security Risk Management Measures and Residential Security Measures, and contributing to security, contingency, evacuation, relocation or business continuity plans and to testing them.

• Demonstrated experience preparing written security analysis, advisories or briefing notes for senior management, and liaising with national law enforcement, the armed forces or civil administration on security matters in Bangladesh.

• Experience conducting physical security or premises assessments and advising on access control, perimeter protection, closed-circuit television and fire safety measures, including oversight of unarmed private security providers and of security communications and personnel-tracking systems.

• Experience delivering security briefings, inductions and training, such as Security Awareness Training, fire safety, first aid, defensive driving or warden training, indicating the audience and the volume.

• Working knowledge of UNSMS and UNDP security policy, including the UN Security Policy Manual (SPM), Security Risk Management (SRM) and Residential Security Measures (RSM), and UNDSS structures, is required, or must be acquired promptly upon engagement.

• Demonstrated experience in a supervisory or team-lead capacity, or clear readiness to provide day-to-day work direction to national security support personnel.

• Proficiency in the use of computers and standard office software (MS Word, Excel and similar) and familiarity with ERP or web-based management systems.

Required Language(s)

• Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

• Fluency in Bangla is required.

 

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination. 

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles. 

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement.  We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement

jobs.title: Head of Organization Development
jobs.description:
Job Description 

 

At our company, we hold an uncompromising stance against mediocrity, committing ourselves to work that delivers audacious impact and is fueled by a pioneering spirit of continuous progress and innovation. This ambition is supported by leadership grounded in courage and clarity—ensuring alignment, accountability, and purpose in everything we do. Integrity shapes how we hire, recognize, and develop talent, with a focus on potential, ambition, and long term growth. Together, we operate with collective strength, prioritizing meaningful results over unnecessary rituals and navigating challenges with unity and resolve. Above all, we remain steadfast and resilient, never losing sight of our commitments and continuously pushing forward through complexity with determination and purpose to create a better life for all. 

 

The Head of Organization Development is a strategic transformation partner. This is not a conventional HR role. You will build the people capability, talent architecture, leadership pipeline, and employer brand that powers Banglalink's strategic digital transformation across five high-growth verticals.

You need a digital-native talent mindset, the ability to design skills-based talent ecosystems, and the commercial conviction to make Banglalink the most sought-after employer for Bangladesh's next generation of digital, technology, and FinTech talent.

 

1. Talent Management

• Design and lead enterprise-wide frameworks for talent identification, succession planning, and leadership pipeline development across businesses verticals.

• Partner with Business Leaders and HR Business Partners to identify critical roles, strengthen succession readiness, and build future talent pipelines through skills-based workforce planning.

• Design programs to develop, engage, and retain talent through coaching, mentoring, cross-functional rotations, and stretch assignments that build future-ready leaders.

• Establish talent governance and analytics — leveraging succession analytics, skills mapping, and predictive people analytics to support data-driven talent decisions.

 

2. Learning & Leadership Development

• Lead the L&D strategy by identifying capability gaps, conducting enterprise-wide Training Needs Analysis, and delivering learning solutions aligned with business priorities.

• Design leadership development frameworks — executive coaching, mentoring, 360° feedback, and high-potential development programs — for emerging, mid-level, and senior leaders.

• Drive a future-ready learning culture through digital learning, AI capability building, and continuous upskilling initiatives.

• Establish learning governance and analytics, measuring business impact and learning effectiveness through digital and AI-enabled platforms.

 

3. Culture

• Lead the culture and employee experience strategy to build a high-performance, inclusive, purpose-driven workplace by embedding company values into everyday practice.

• Lead culture transformation initiatives — employee engagement, change management, and recognition — that strengthen collaboration, innovation, and business performance.

• Partner with Business Leaders and HR Business Partners on employee listening, engagement surveys, and culture diagnostics to improve organizational health.

• Provide strategic culture insights through engagement analytics and workforce sentiment dashboards to support executive decision-making.

 

4. Employer Branding

• Own the Employer Branding strategy, defining and strengthening the Employee Value Proposition (EVP) to position the company as an employer of choice.

• Drive integrated branding initiatives across digital platforms, social media, university partnerships, and corporate events to build employer reputation.

• Partner with Talent Acquisition and Corporate Communications to deliver consistent brand experience across the employee lifecycle.

• Lead branding governance and analytics — measuring EVP effectiveness, employer brand perception, and industry benchmarking.

Academic Qualification

• BBA/MBA with specialization in Human Resource

Job Experience Required

• 10-12 years of relevant experience with at least 5-6 years’ experience in a leading Talent & Organization Development role

Required Capabilities

• Deep expertise in modern talent management: skills-based talent models, Critical Roles/Persons frameworks, succession architecture, and HIPO program design in a large or fast-growing organization.

• Digital transformation fluency — experience designing HR interventions for technology, FinTech, or platform businesses; comfortable with agile working models and digital product organizations.

• Learning architecture expertise: LXP/LMS platforms, AI-powered learning design, blended ecosystems, and rigorous L&D measurement (Kirkpatrick + ROI).

• Employer branding hands-on: LinkedIn Talent Insights, Glassdoor management, university partnerships, Top Employer / GPTW certification experience.

• People analytics capability: Power BI, Tableau, Visier, or equivalent — able to build dashboards and translate data into CEO-ready decisions.

• Change management experience — ideally from large-scale digital transformation or M&A-driven organizational change.

• Executive-level stakeholder management and influencing; able to align across matrix structures and VEON Group governance.

• Outstanding communication and leadership presence — operates credibly at CEO-1 and CEO-2 levels without hand-holding.

jobs.title: Android Developer (Native)
jobs.description:
Inument Solutions (www.inument.com) is a software outsourcing company headquartered in Singapore, with its Engineering Hub in Dhaka. We work with clients from Australia and Europe.

At Inument, we are looking for a skilled Native Android Developer with strong, recent hands-on experience in Android application development. You will work on building reliable, high-performance Android apps using modern Android frameworks and best practices for international clients.

Job Details:

• Workplace: On-site

• Working Hours: 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM (Dhaka Time), Sunday to Thursday

• Vacancies: 1

• Experience Required: 3 – 6 years (minimum 3 years of recent, solid experience in Native Android)

• Salary: BDT 80,000 – 150,000/monthly (Negotiable based on skills and experience)

• Must-Have: Strong recent experience in Native Android development (Kotlin). Experience working with outsourcing is a plus.

Job Description:

• Design, develop, and maintain high-quality Android applications.

• Build clean, scalable, and maintainable code following best practices.

• Work with Android SDK, Jetpack components, and modern Android architecture.

• Implement UI/UX designs with pixel-perfect accuracy and smooth performance.

• Integrate RESTful APIs, third-party SDKs, and backend services.

• Contribute to the design and implementation of scalable mobile application architecture, collaborating on system design decisions for high-traffic, large-scale production systems.

• Handle app lifecycle management, performance optimization, and memory management.

• Debug, troubleshoot, and resolve issues across different Android devices and OS versions.

• Collaborate with backend, QA, and product teams to deliver reliable solutions.

• Participate in code reviews and contribute to technical decisions.

• Communicate with international clients to understand requirements and provide updates.

Additional Job Requirements:

• Strong proficiency in Kotlin (Java experience is a plus).

• Solid understanding of Android architecture patterns (MVVM/MVP/Clean Architecture).

• Experience with Jetpack components (ViewModel, LiveData, Room, Navigation, etc.)

• Knowledge of background processing, notifications, and offline storage.

• Experience with Git and collaborative development workflows.

• Familiarity with app publishing, versioning, and Play Store release process.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

• Ability to work independently and within a team with minimal supervision.

Education:

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.

Benefits:

• Two festival bonuses per year.

• Subsidized lunch and snacks. 

• Regular indoor and outdoor team events.

• Frequent knowledge-sharing sessions.

• Long-term growth opportunities in a high-quality work environment.

• Friendly, fun-loving team culture with a competitive salary package.

jobs.description:
About the Role

Inument Solutions is a Singapore-headquartered AI transformation and technology company with its Engineering Hub in Dhaka. We build software services and SaaS products for startups and enterprises across Australia and Europe.

Shopiment builds and runs apps on the Shopify App Store. Two products are currently live — Flexibar (announcement bars) and Gratify (loyalty and rewards), used by merchants in more than 50 countries, with additional products in the pipeline.

Our products are primarily self-serve and freemium. A merchant discovers an app, installs it, sets it up, experiences its value, and decides whether to upgrade. Every step of that journey represents an opportunity to improve activation, engagement, retention, and conversion.

We are looking for a Junior Growth Product Manager who is curious about products, users, data, and growth. This is a hands-on role for someone with 1–3 years of experience who wants to develop strong product and growth skills by working directly on real SaaS products.

You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Business teams to understand user behavior, identify growth opportunities, support experiments, and turn insights into practical product improvements.

Job Details

• Workplace: On-site, Baridhara DOHS, Dhaka

• Working Days: Monday – Friday

• Weekends: Saturday – Sunday

• Position: Junior Growth Product Manager

• Experience Required: 1–3 years

• Salary: BDT 20,000 – BDT 35,000 monthly gross

• Vacancies: 1

• Employment Type: Full-time

Job Description

• Analyze the merchant journey across discovery, installation, onboarding, activation, engagement, and upgrade.

• Help identify where users drop off and work with the team to understand why.

• Support the definition and tracking of important product and growth metrics.

• Research competitors, market trends, Shopify merchants, and customer needs.

• Conduct user research and turn findings into actionable product recommendations.

• Support the planning and execution of growth experiments with clear hypotheses and measurable outcomes.

• Work with Product and Engineering teams to convert ideas into clear requirements, user stories, and specifications.

• Monitor experiment results and help determine whether an initiative should be continued, improved, or stopped.

• Support App Store review and feedback analysis to identify recurring customer needs and product opportunities.

• Help improve onboarding, activation, retention, and conversion across Shopiment products.

• Work with Marketing and Business teams to connect product improvements with acquisition and growth initiatives.

• Use AI tools, analytics, research, and modern productivity tools to work faster and make better decisions.

• Maintain clear documentation of research, experiments, findings, and recommendations.

What We’re Looking For

• 1–3 years of experience in product management, product growth, growth marketing, business analysis, digital products, SaaS, or a related field.

• Genuine interest in product development, user behavior, SaaS, and growth.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Comfortable working with data and asking the right questions about metrics.

• Ability to conduct independent research and develop a clear point of view.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving ability.

• Ability to break down an unclear problem into practical next steps.

• Comfortable working with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Business teams.

• Willingness to experiment, learn from failure, and continuously improve.

• Strong ownership, curiosity, and attention to detail.

• Comfortable using AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or similar tools.

Strong Plus

• Experience working with a SaaS or self-serve digital product.

• Experience with Google Analytics, Mixpanel, Amplitude, PostHog, or similar platforms.

• Experience conducting user interviews, surveys, or customer research.

• Familiarity with A/B testing and growth experimentation.

• Experience with Shopify, Shopify Apps, e-commerce, or merchant-facing products.

• Experience working with freemium or subscription-based products.

• Basic understanding of APIs, software development workflows, or technical product management.

• Experience building or managing a user community.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

You don’t need to know everything about product management.

You need to be curious enough to investigate, analytical enough to understand what the data is saying, and proactive enough to turn what you learn into action.

You should enjoy asking:

Why are users dropping off?
What can we improve?
How do we know it worked?

If you enjoy understanding users, solving product problems, testing ideas, and learning how digital products grow, this role could be a strong starting point for your product career.

Why Join Shopiment?

• Work directly on live Shopify SaaS products used by merchants across multiple countries.

• Gain practical experience across Product Management, Growth, SaaS, Analytics, User Research, and Experimentation.

• Work closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Business teams.

• Learn how self-serve and freemium products acquire, activate, retain, and convert users.

• Get exposure to real product decisions rather than only theoretical assignments.

• Work with AI tools and modern product-growth workflows.

• Build a strong foundation for a long-term career in Product Management and Growth.

• Grow based on your learning, ownership, and performance.

Education

A Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, Economics, Marketing, Engineering, or a related discipline is preferred.

However, academic background alone will not determine your suitability. We value curiosity, analytical thinking, communication, ownership, and demonstrated ability to learn.

How to Apply

Send your CV to jobs@inument.com with your expected salary.

<position>_<years of experience>_<expected salary>_<university>

Junior Growth Product Manager_3_50K_NSU

jobs.title: Sales Development Representative
jobs.description:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We are looking for a driven and highly communicative Sales Development Representative (SDR) to join our growing Sales team in Bangladesh.

As an SDR, you will be responsible for creating new sales opportunities by identifying and engaging potential customers, understanding their needs, introducing them to our solutions, and booking qualified product demonstration meetings for our Account Executives. This is a high impact, target driven role where your ability to communicate confidently, build relationships, learn quickly, and persist through challenges will directly contribute to our sales growth. • Process Automation: Develop automated scripts, webhooks, and API integrations that connect disparate data sources and streamline cross-functional business operations without manual oversight.

• Cross-Functional Strategy: Act as a technical liaison between operations, product, and core data engineering teams to consolidate ambient data streams and enforce system reliability.

• Hands-on experience with version control (Git) and CI/CD workflows is strictly required.

• Experience with internal tool builders (e.g., Retool) and modern deployment platforms (e.g., Vercel) is highly advantageous.
